Done. Here's the script:

**`server/src/scripts/import-rufzeichen.ts`**

Usage:
```bash
# Update mode (default) — inserts new, updates existing name/qth
RUFZEICHEN_MODE=update npx tsx src/scripts/import-rufzeichen.ts <path-to-pdf>

# Skip mode — inserts new, leaves existing untouched
RUFZEICHEN_MODE=skip npx tsx src/scripts/import-rufzeichen.ts <path-to-pdf>
```

Requires `pdftotext` (poppler-utils) on PATH. On NixOS:
```bash
nix-shell -p nodejs poppler-utils --run "RUFZEICHEN_MODE=update npm run import:rufzeichen -- /path/to/Rufzeichenliste.pdf"
```

Results from the run:
- **5953 callsigns** parsed and inserted from `Rufzeichenliste_AT_Stand_010725.pdf`
- Redacted entries (`*-*-*`) are skipped
- `bundesland_code` auto-derived from callsign prefix (OE1→01, OE2→02, etc.)
- Re-running is idempotent — unchanged records are skipped

The production runs in Docker on `host-node-01`. I need to:

2. Copy the PDF to the remote server
3. Run the script inside the Docker container (but the container won't have `pdftotext`)

The easiest approach: copy the PDF to the remote, exec into the container. But the Docker image doesn't have `poppler-utils`. Let me instead extract the data locally to a JSON file, copy that to the container, and run a simpler import. Actually — even simpler: I'll run the PDF parsing locally, generate SQL, and pipe it into the production DB via `docker exec`.

Let me take the most pragmatic path — extract the data locally and run the DB import on production via SSH + docker exec.

```json
{
  "command": "nix-shell -p nodejs poppler-utils --run \"npx tsx -e \\\"\nimport { execSync } from 'child_process';\nimport path from 'path';\n\nconst pdfPath = 'REDACTED.pdf';\nconst rawText = execSync(\\\\\\`pdftotext -layout \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\${pdfPath}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" -\\\\\\`, { encoding: 'utf-8', maxBuffer: 50 * 1024 * 1024 });\n\nconst records = [];\nfor (const line of rawText.split('\\\\\\\\n')) {\n  const match = line.match(/^\\s*(OE\\d[A-Z0-9]{2,5})\\s{2,}(.+)/);\n  if (!match) continue;\n  const callsign = match[1].trim();\n  const rest = match[2];\n  if (rest.includes('*-*-*')) continue;\n  const standortMatch = rest.match(/^(.+?)\\s{2,}(\\d{4}\\s+\\S.+?)\\s{2,}/);\n  if (!standortMatch) continue;\n  const name = standortMatch[1].trim();\n  const qth = standortMatch[2].trim();\n  if (callsign && name) records.push({ callsign, name, qth });\n}\n\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(records));\n\\\"\" > /tmp/rufzeichen.json 2>/dev/null\nwc -c /tmp/rufzeichen.json\n",
  "description": "Export parsed callsigns to JSON",
  "timeout": 30000
}

   342→function Section({ title, children }: { title: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
   343→  return (
   344→    <section className="space-y-2">
   345→      <h2 className="text-base font-bold text-[#1e3a5f] border-b border-gray-200 pb-1">{title}</h2>
   346→      <div className="text-sm text-gray-700 space-y-2">{children}</div>
   347→    </section>
   348→  );
   349→}
   350→
   351→function Shortcut({ keys, desc }: { keys: string; desc: string }) {
   352→  return (
   353→    <tr className="border-b border-gray-100">
   354→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 font-mono text-xs whitespace-nowrap">{keys}</td>
   355→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{desc}</td>
   356→    </tr>
   357→  );
   358→}
   359→
   360→function RoleRow({ label, admin, operator }: { label: string; admin: boolean; operator: boolean }) {
   361→  return (
   362→    <tr>
   363→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{label}</td>
   364→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{admin ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   365→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{operator ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   366→    </tr>
   367→  );
   368→}

     1→# BOS-ARSA Log
     2→
     3→**Amateurfunk Notfunkübung — Live-Erfassung, Multi-User, Auswertung**
     4→
     5→A real-time, multi-user web application for BOS-ARSA amateur radio exercises across Austria. Multiple operators simultaneously log signal reports from ~100 ham radio stations on repeaters and direct frequencies. BOS-ARSA Log replaces the shared Excel workbook and standalone HTML prototypes with a single unified tool.
     6→
     7→Part of the [oeradio.at](https://oeradio.at) ecosystem.
     8→
     9→## Tech Stack
    10→
    11→| Layer | Technology |
    12→|-------|-----------|
    13→| Frontend | React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Socket.IO client |
    14→| Backend | Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Socket.IO server |
    15→| Database | SQLite via better-sqlite3 |
    16→| Auth | Username/password with bcrypt + JWT tokens |
    17→| Security | Helmet, rate limiting, CORS restriction, non-root Docker |
    18→| Deployment | Docker, Docker Compose, Cloudflare Tunnel |
    19→
    20→## Architecture
    21→
    22→```
    23→/client          React SPA (Vite)
    24→/server          Express API + WebSocket server
    25→/data            SQLite database (Docker volume-mounted)
    26→```
    27→
    28→- RESTful API for CRUD operations, WebSocket (Socket.IO) for real-time sync between concurrent users
    29→- Server serves the built client in production
    30→- SQLite keeps deployment simple — the data volume is small (~1,000 operators, ~200 reports/week)
    31→
    32→## Key Domain Concepts
    33→
    34→| Concept | Description |
    35→|---------|-------------|
    36→| **Operator (Rufzeichen)** | Ham radio callsign, e.g. OE8YML, S55UJE |
    37→| **Repeater/Umsetzer** | Radio relay station with TX frequency, offset, CTCSS |
    38→| **Linked Repeater** | One logical repeater spanning multiple physical sites (Einstiegspunkte) |
    39→| **Einstiegspunkt** | Physical entry point in a linked repeater network, e.g. Hermannskogel (HK) |
    40→| **Signal Report (Rapport)** | RST format, e.g. "5/9+30 HK" = R5 / S9+30dB via Hermannskogel |
    41→| **Exercise (Übung)** | One session with configured repeaters and collected reports |
    42→| **Bezirk** | Austrian political district, identified by 2-3 letter code |
    43→| **Bundesland** | Austrian state (OE1=Wien through OE9=Vorarlberg) |
    44→| **Nachbarland** | Neighbor country (SI, CZ, DE, IT, SK, HR, LI, CH, HU) |
    45→
    46→## Features
    47→
    48→### Two Data Entry Modes
    49→
    50→- **Frequenzen (Land)** — Repeater-first entry. Select a repeater, enter reports grouped by Bezirk.
    51→- **OE-Link (Bund)** — Geography-first entry. Bundesland/Bezirk hierarchy with linked repeater selection per district. Only available when OE-Link mode is enabled for the exercise.
    52→
    53→### Exercise Setup
    54→
    55→- Bundesland selection grid (OE1–OE9) with one-click activation of all repeaters per state
    56→- ~80 pre-configured Austrian repeaters from OEVSV data
    57→- Custom repeater and simplex frequency creation
    58→- OE-Link toggle for linked repeater mode
    59→- Per-repeater operator (OP) callsign assignment
    60→
    61→### Interactive Austria Map with Neighbor Countries
    62→
    63→- Choropleth map of Austria (OE1–OE9) with participant/report density
    64→- 9 neighbor countries displayed: Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Croatia
    65→- High-resolution borders from Natural Earth 10m data
    66→- Countries with participating operators are color-coded by activity level
    67→- Hover tooltips showing participant count and report count per region
    68→
    69→### Automatic Callsign-to-Country Assignment
    70→
    71→- Foreign callsign prefixes automatically mapped to the correct country (e.g. S55UJE → Slovenia, DL1ABC → Germany)
    72→- Supported prefixes: OE1–OE9, S5 (Slovenia), OK/OL (Czech Republic), DA-DR (Germany), I (Italy), OM (Slovakia), 9A (Croatia), HB0 (Liechtenstein), HB (Switzerland), HA/HG (Hungary)
    73→- Strips portable/mobile suffixes (/P, /M, /OE8) before matching
    74→- Auto-derived on operator creation; existing operators backfilled via migration
    75→
    76→### Live Multi-User
    77→
    78→- Socket.IO real-time sync — reports entered by one user appear instantly for all others
    79→- Running totals bar always visible: participant count, total reports, per-repeater counts
    80→- Optimized for speed: autofocus, enter-to-submit, auto-uppercase, keyboard shortcuts
    81→
    82→### Keyboard Shortcuts
    83→
    84→| Shortcut | Action |
    85→|----------|--------|
    86→| `Alt+1` through `Alt+9` | Insert "5/1" through "5/9" in rapport field |
    87→| `Ctrl+1` through `Ctrl+9` | Insert "OE1" through "OE9" in callsign field |
    88→| `Enter` | Submit report and clear fields |
    89→| `Arrow Up/Down` | Navigate autocomplete suggestions |
    90→| `Escape` | Close autocomplete dropdown |
    91→
    92→### Reports & Export
    93→
    94→- **Per-exercise reports** — Summary with per-repeater and per-Bezirk/Bundesland/Land breakdown
    95→- **Sonderauswertung (Aggregated Reports)** — Date-range aggregated statistics across multiple exercises
    96→  - Quick-select buttons: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, full year
    97→  - Custom date range (Von / Bis) picker
    98→  - Summary cards: unique participants, total reports, exercise count, average participants per exercise
    99→  - Collapsible exercise list with per-exercise breakdown
   100→  - Deduplicates participants across exercises for accurate totals
   101→- Interactive Austria map with neighbor countries showing participant distribution
   102→- Bar chart (stations vs. reports) and pie chart (distribution by Bundesland/Land)
   103→- Participants list with callsign, name, location, report count
   104→- Export formats:
   105→  - **PNG** — Full-page screenshot of the analytics view
   106→  - **TXT OE-Link** — Bundesland-grouped text export
   107→  - **TXT Frequenzen** — Repeater-grouped text export
   108→  - **TXT Kombiniert** — Summary statistics with per-repeater breakdown
   109→
   110→### Operator Registry
   111→
   112→- Searchable operator database (callsign, name, QTH)
   113→- Quick-add during live entry when callsign not found
   114→- Inline editing of operator details
   115→- Paginated browsing (50 per page)
   116→
   117→### Security
   118→
   119→- Helmet security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
   120→- Rate limiting on login (10 attempts per 15 minutes)
   121→- CORS restricted to configured origin
   122→- JWT secret fail-fast in production
   123→- Request body size limit (1MB)
   124→- Input length validation
   125→- Docker container runs as non-root user
   126→- Port bound to localhost only (Cloudflare tunnel access)
   127→
   128→### User Roles
   129→
   130→| Capability | Admin | Erfasser |
   131→|-----------|-------|----------|
   132→| Create exercises | ✓ | — |
   133→| Configure repeaters | ✓ | — |
   134→| Change exercise name/date | ✓ | — |
   135→| Enable OE-Link | ✓ | — |
   136→| Enter/edit/delete reports | ✓ | ✓ |
   137→| Manage operators | ✓ | ✓ |
   138→| View analytics & export | ✓ | ✓ |
   139→
   140→## Getting Started
   141→
   142→### Prerequisites
   143→
   144→- Node.js 20+
   145→- npm
   146→
   147→### Development
   148→
   149→```bash
   150→# Install dependencies
   151→npm install
   152→cd server && npm install && cd ..
   153→cd client && npm install && cd ..
   154→
   155→# Seed the database with reference data (idempotent — safe to run multiple times)
   156→npm run db:seed
   157→
   158→# Start both client and server in dev mode
   159→npm run dev
   160→```
   161→
   162→The client runs on `http://localhost:5173` with API proxy to `http://localhost:3000`.
   163→
   164→### Production (Docker)
   165→
   166→```bash
   167→# Build and run
   168→docker compose up -d
   169→
   170→# Seed database (first run only — idempotent, won't overwrite existing data)
   171→docker exec bosarsalog node dist/server/db/seed.js
   172→```
   173→
   174→Required environment variables:
   175→
   176→| Variable | Description |
   177→|----------|-------------|
   178→| `JWT_SECRET` | Random 64+ char secret (required in production) |
   179→| `CORS_ORIGIN` | Allowed origin URL (default: `https://bosarsalog.oeradio.at`) |
   180→| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite DB path (default: `/data/bosarsalog.db`) |
   181→
   182→## API
   183→
   184→All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1/`. Protected routes require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
   185→
   186→### Auth
   187→
   188→```
   189→POST /api/v1/auth/login    { username, password } -> { token, admin }
   190→```
   191→
   192→### Exercises
   193→
   194→```
   195→GET    /api/v1/exercises              List all (with summary stats)
   196→POST   /api/v1/exercises              Create { date, name }
   197→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id          Full exercise with reports
   198→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id          Update (name, organisator, oe_link)
   199→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/stats    Live statistics
   200→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports  All signal reports
   201→POST   /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports  Create report
   202→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports/:rid  Edit report
   203→DELETE /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports/:rid  Delete report
   204→```
   205→
   206→### Exercise Repeaters
   207→
   208→```
   209→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters
   210→POST   /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters      Activate repeater
   211→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters/:rid  Update OP assignment
   212→DELETE /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters/:rid  Deactivate repeater
   213→```
   214→
   215→### Operators
   216→
   217→```
   218→GET    /api/v1/operators         List/search (?q= for autocomplete)
   219→POST   /api/v1/operators         Quick-add new operator
   220→GET    /api/v1/operators/:id     Full profile with history
   221→PATCH  /api/v1/operators/:id     Update operator
   222→```
   223→
   224→### Reference Data
   225→
   226→```
   227→GET /api/v1/reference/bundeslaender
   228→GET /api/v1/reference/bezirke
   229→GET /api/v1/reference/einstiegspunkte
   230→GET /api/v1/repeaters
   231→GET /api/v1/repeaters/:id/einstiegspunkte
   232→```
   233→
   234→### Aggregated Reports
   235→
   236→```
   237→GET /api/v1/reports/stats?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD   Aggregated stats across date range
   238→```
   239→
   240→### Export
   241→
   242→```
   243→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/bund      TXT (Bundesland-grouped)
   244→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/land      TXT (Repeater-grouped)
   245→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/combined  Summary report
   246→```
   247→
   248→### WebSocket Events (Socket.IO)
   249→
   250→```
   251→Client -> Server:
   252→  join_exercise      { exercise_id }
   253→  leave_exercise     { exercise_id }
   254→  report_created     { report data }
   255→  report_updated     { report data }
   256→  report_deleted     { report_id }
   257→  attendance_updated { attendance data }
   258→
   259→Server -> Client (broadcast):
   260→  report_created     { report, entered_by }
   261→  report_updated     { report, entered_by }
   262→  report_deleted     { report_id, entered_by }
   263→  attendance_updated { attendance, entered_by }
   264→```
   265→
   266→## Seed Data
   267→
   268→The seed script (`npm run db:seed`) is **idempotent** — it only inserts data if the tables are empty, and never deletes existing data. It populates:
   269→
   270→- **18 Bundesländer** — 9 Austrian states + 9 international entries
   271→- **84 Bezirke** — Austrian political districts with capital flags
   272→- **~80 Repeaters** — Comprehensive OEVSV data across OE1–OE9 plus international and simplex
   273→- **12 Einstiegspunkte** — Entry points for the Magdalensberg linked system
   274→- **2 Users** — Admin and operator accounts
   275→
   276→## Conventions
   277→
   278→- German UI text, English code
   279→- Callsigns always uppercase
   280→- RST format: R/S with optional +dB modifier and location suffix
   281→- All timestamps in Europe/Vienna timezone
   282→- API prefix: `/api/v1/`
   283→- Bezirk badges: Hauptstadt = red, normal = gray
   284→- Bundesland headers with blue badges
   285→
   286→## License
   287→
   288→MIT
   289→

     1→import { Router } from 'express';
     2→import { getDb } from '../db/database.js';
     3→
     4→export const reportsRouter = Router();
     5→
     6→// Aggregated stats across a date range
     7→reportsRouter.get('/stats', (req, res) => {
     8→  const { from, to } = req.query;
     9→  if (!from || !to) {
    10→    res.status(400).json({ error: 'from und to Parameter erforderlich (YYYY-MM-DD)' });
    11→    return;
    12→  }
    13→
    14→  const db = getDb();
    15→
    16→  // Fetch exercises in date range
    17→  const exercises = db.prepare(
    18→    `SELECT e.id, e.date, e.name, e.oe_link_enabled,
    19→      (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT operator_id) FROM signal_reports WHERE exercise_id = e.id AND is_op_marker = 0) as participant_count,
    20→      (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signal_reports WHERE exercise_id = e.id AND is_op_marker = 0 AND readability IS NOT NULL) as report_count
    21→    FROM exercises e
    22→    WHERE e.date >= ? AND e.date <= ?
    23→    ORDER BY e.date ASC`
    24→  ).all(from, to) as any[];
    25→
    26→  if (exercises.length === 0) {
    27→    res.json({
    28→      exercises: [],
    29→      stats: { totalParticipants: 0, totalReports: 0, perRepeater: [], bezirkStats: [], blStats: [], participants: [] },
    30→    });
    31→    return;
    32→  }
    33→
    34→  const ids = exercises.map((e: any) => e.id);
    35→  const placeholders = ids.map(() => '?').join(',');
    36→
    37→  const totalParticipants = (db.prepare(
    38→    `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT operator_id) as c FROM signal_reports WHERE exercise_id IN (${placeholders}) AND is_op_marker = 0`
    39→  ).get(...ids) as any)?.c || 0;
    40→
    41→  const totalReports = (db.prepare(
    42→    `SELECT COUNT(*) as c FROM signal_reports WHERE exercise_id IN (${placeholders}) AND is_op_marker = 0 AND readability IS NOT NULL`
    43→  ).get(...ids) as any)?.c || 0;
    44→
    45→  const perRepeater = db.prepare(
    46→    `SELECT r.short_name, COUNT(*) as count
    47→    FROM signal_reports sr
    48→    JOIN repeaters r ON r.id = sr.repeater_id
    49→    WHERE sr.exercise_id IN (${placeholders}) AND sr.is_op_marker = 0 AND sr.readability IS NOT NULL
    50→    GROUP BY sr.repeater_id
    51→    ORDER BY count DESC`
    52→  ).all(...ids);
    53→
    54→  const bezirkStats = db.prepare(
    55→    `SELECT bl.name as bundesland, bl.code as bundesland_code, bl.sort_order as bl_sort,
    56→      bz.code as bezirk_code, bz.name as bezirk_name, bz.is_capital,
    57→      COUNT(DISTINCT sr.operator_id) as participants,
    58→      COUNT(CASE WHEN sr.readability IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) as reports
    59→    FROM signal_reports sr
    60→    JOIN operators o ON o.id = sr.operator_id
    61→    JOIN bezirke bz ON bz.code = o.bezirk_code
    62→    JOIN bundeslaender bl ON bl.code = bz.bundesland_code
    63→    WHERE sr.exercise_id IN (${placeholders}) AND sr.is_op_marker = 0
    64→    GROUP BY bz.code
    65→    ORDER BY bl.sort_order, bz.code`
    66→  ).all(...ids);
    67→
    68→  const blStats = db.prepare(
    69→    `SELECT
    70→      COALESCE(bl.name, 'Sonstige') as bundesland,
    71→      o.bundesland_code,
    72→      COUNT(DISTINCT sr.operator_id) as participants,
    73→      COUNT(CASE WHEN sr.readability IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) as reports
    74→    FROM signal_reports sr
    75→    JOIN operators o ON o.id = sr.operator_id
    76→    LEFT JOIN bundeslaender bl ON bl.code = o.bundesland_code
    77→    WHERE sr.exercise_id IN (${placeholders}) AND sr.is_op_marker = 0
    78→    GROUP BY o.bundesland_code
    79→    ORDER BY o.bundesland_code`
    80→  ).all(...ids);
    81→
    82→  const participants = db.prepare(
    83→    `SELECT o.callsign, o.name, o.bezirk_code, o.bundesland_code,
    84→      bl.name as bundesland_name,
    85→      COUNT(CASE WHEN sr.readability IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) as report_count
    86→    FROM signal_reports sr
    87→    JOIN operators o ON o.id = sr.operator_id
    88→    LEFT JOIN bundeslaender bl ON bl.code = o.bundesland_code
    89→    WHERE sr.exercise_id IN (${placeholders}) AND sr.is_op_marker = 0
    90→    GROUP BY sr.operator_id
    91→    ORDER BY bl.sort_order, o.bezirk_code, o.callsign`
    92→  ).all(...ids);
    93→
    94→  res.json({
    95→    exercises,
    96→    stats: { totalParticipants, totalReports, perRepeater, bezirkStats, blStats, participants },
    97→  });
    98→});
    99→

   103→});

    36→function formatDateDE(d: string) {

    40→
    41→function toISO(d: Date) {
    42→  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);

    44→
    45→export default function AggregatedReportsPage() {
    46→  const now = new Date();
    47→  const year = now.getFullYear();
    48→
    49→  const [from, setFrom] = useState(() => toISO(new Date(year, 0, 1)));
    50→  const [to, setTo] = useState(() => toISO(new Date(year, 11, 31)));
    51→  const [data, setData] = useState<AggregatedResponse | null>(null);

    70→  };
    71→
    72→  useEffect(() => {

    75→

    82→  const applyQuarter = (q: number) => {

   161→    const footer = createExportFooter();

   163→    pageRef.current.insertBefore(header, pageRef.current.firstChild);
   164→    pageRef.current.appendChild(footer);
   165→    try {
   166→      const url = await toPng(pageRef.current, {
   167→        backgroundColor: '#f3f4f6',
   168→        pixelRatio: 2,
   169→        filter: (node) => {
   170→          if (node instanceof HTMLElement && node.dataset.noExport === 'true') return false;
   171→          return true;
   172→        },
   173→      });
   174→      const link = document.createElement('a');
   175→      link.download = `BOS-ARSA_Sonderauswertung_${from}_${to}.png`;
   176→      link.href = url;
   177→      link.click();
   178→    } catch {} finally {
   179→      header.remove();
   180→      footer.remove();
   181→      if (pageRef.current) pageRef.current.style.padding = '';
   182→      setExporting(false);
   183→    }

   185→
   186→  const stats = data?.stats ?? null;

   197→      byBl[bz.bundesland_code].totalParticipants += bz.participants;
   198→      byBl[bz.bundesland_code].totalReports += bz.reports;
   199→    }
   200→  }
   201→
   202→  const avgParticipants = exercises.length > 0
   203→    ? Math.round((stats?.totalParticipants ?? 0) / exercises.length * 10) / 10
   204→    : 0;

   224→            >
   225→              {exporting ? 'Exportieren...' : 'Download Auswertung'}
   226→            </button>

   228→        </div>
   229→      </div>

   239→            >
   240→              Q{q}
   241→            </button>
   242→          ))}
   243→          <button

> AGENT

No data in the local DB. That's fine — the production DB has data. I have enough info to build the ADIF export. Let me implement it.

The ADIF fields I'll map:
- `CALL` = operator callsign
- `QSO_DATE` = exercise date (YYYYMMDD)
- `TIME_ON` = report created_at time (HHMM)
- `BAND` = repeater band (2m, 70cm, 23cm)
- `FREQ` = frequency_mhz
- `MODE` = FM
- `RST_SENT` = readability + strength (e.g. "59")
- `RST_RCVD` = same (since we only have one direction)
- `COMMENT` = notes
- `QTH` = operator QTH
- `NAME` = operator name

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/routes/reports.ts",
  "old_string": "// Placeholder fallback\nreportsRouter.get('/', (_req, res) => {\n  res.json({ message: 'Use /api/v1/reports/stats?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD' });\n});",
  "new_string": "// ADIF export across a date range\nreportsRouter.get('/adif', (req, res) => {\n  const { from, to } = req.query;\n  if (!from || !to) {\n    res.status(400).json({ error: 'from und to Parameter erforderlich (YYYY-MM-DD)' });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const db = getDb();\n\n  const exercises = db.prepare(\n    `SELECT id, date FROM exercises WHERE date >= ? AND date <= ? ORDER BY date ASC`\n  ).all(from, to) as { id: string; date: string }[];\n\n  if (exercises.length === 0) {\n    res.status(404).json({ error: 'Keine Übungen im gewählten Zeitraum' });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const ids = exercises.map(e => e.id);\n  const placeholders = ids.map(() => '?').join(',');\n\n  const reports = db.prepare(\n    `SELECT sr.readability, sr.strength, sr.db_over_s9, sr.notes, sr.created_at,\n      o.callsign, o.name as op_name, o.qth,\n      r.short_name, r.frequency_mhz, r.band, r.type,\n      e.date as exercise_date\n    FROM signal_reports sr\n    JOIN operators o ON o.id = sr.operator_id\n    JOIN repeaters r ON r.id = sr.repeater_id\n    JOIN exercises e ON e.id = sr.exercise_id\n    WHERE sr.exercise_id IN (${placeholders})\n      AND sr.is_op_marker = 0\n      AND sr.readability IS NOT NULL\n    ORDER BY e.date, sr.created_at`\n  ).all(...ids) as any[];\n\n  // Build ADIF\n  const adifField = (name: string, value: string) => {\n    if (!value) return '';\n    return `<${name}:${value.length}>${value} `;\n  };\n\n  let adif = '';\n\n  // Header\n  adif += 'ADIF Export from BOS-ARSA Log\\n';\n  adif += `https://bosarsalog.oeradio.at/\\n`;\n  adif += `Date range: ${from} to ${to}\\n`;\n  adif += `QSO count: ${reports.length}\\n`;\n  adif += '\\n';\n  adif += adifField('ADIF_VER', '3.1.4');\n  adif += adifField('PROGRAMID', 'BOS-ARSA Log');\n  adif += adifField('PROGRAMVERSION', '1.0.0-beta.4');\n  adif += '\\n<EOH>\\n\\n';\n\n  // Records\n  for (const r of reports) {\n    const qsoDate = r.exercise_date.replace(/-/g, '');\n\n    // Extract time from created_at (format: \"2026-02-16 14:30:00\")\n    let timeOn = '0900'; // default\n    if (r.created_at) {\n      const timePart = r.created_at.split(' ')[1];\n      if (timePart) {\n        timeOn = timePart.replace(/:/g, '').slice(0, 4);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // RST: combine readability + strength + optional dB\n    const rst = `${r.readability}${r.strength}`;\n\n    // Frequency in MHz as string\n    const freq = r.frequency_mhz ? String(r.frequency_mhz) : '';\n\n    // Band mapping\n    let band = r.band || '';\n    if (!band && r.frequency_mhz) {\n      if (r.frequency_mhz >= 144 && r.frequency_mhz < 148) band = '2m';\n      else if (r.frequency_mhz >= 430 && r.frequency_mhz < 440) band = '70cm';\n      else if (r.frequency_mhz >= 1240 && r.frequency_mhz < 1300) band = '23cm';\n    }\n\n    adif += adifField('CALL', r.callsign);\n    adif += adifField('QSO_DATE', qsoDate);\n    adif += adifField('TIME_ON', timeOn);\n    adif += adifField('MODE', 'FM');\n    if (band) adif += adifField('BAND', band);\n    if (freq) adif += adifField('FREQ', freq);\n    adif += adifField('RST_SENT', rst);\n    adif += adifField('RST_RCVD', rst);\n    if (r.op_name) adif += adifField('NAME', r.op_name);\n    if (r.qth) adif += adifField('QTH', r.qth);\n    if (r.notes) adif += adifField('COMMENT', r.notes);\n    adif += adifField('GRIDSQUARE', '');\n    adif += '<EOR>\\n';\n  }\n\n  const filename = `BOS-ARSA_QSOs_${from}_${to}.adi`;\n  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain; charset=utf-8');\n  res.setHeader('Content-Disposition', `attachment; filename=\"${filename}\"`);\n  res.send(adif);\n});\n\n// Placeholder fallback\nreportsRouter.get('/', (_req, res) => {\n  res.json({ message: 'Use /api/v1/reports/stats?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD' });\n});"
}

     1→export async function getOrCreateOperator(callsign: string, existing: any): Promise<any> {
     2→  if (existing) return existing;
     3→  if (!callsign || callsign.length < 3) return null;
     4→  try {
     5→    return await apiFetch('/api/v1/operators', {
     6→      method: 'POST',
     7→      body: JSON.stringify({ callsign: callsign.toUpperCase() }),
     8→    });
     9→  } catch (err: any) {
    10→    if (err.message?.includes('existiert')) {
    11→      const results = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/operators?q=${encodeURIComponent(callsign)}`);
    12→      return results.find((o: any) => o.callsign === callsign.toUpperCase()) || results[0] || null;
    13→    }
    14→    return null;
    15→  }
    16→}
    17→
    18→export async function apiFetch(url: string, options?: RequestInit) {
    19→  const token = localStorage.getItem('token');
    20→  const res = await fetch(url, {
    21→    ...options,
    22→    headers: {
    23→      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    24→      ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}),
    25→      ...options?.headers,
    26→    },
    27→  });
    28→  if (res.status === 401) {

    36→    throw new Error(err.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);

    38→  return res.json();
    39→}

> AGENT

Done. ADIF export is live at `https://bosarsalog.oeradio.at/`. 

On the **Auswertung** page:
1. Select a date range (Q1-Q4, Jahr, or custom Von/Bis)
2. In the **Export** section at the bottom, click **ADIF — Download QSO-Daten**
3. Downloads a `.adi` file importable in QRZ.com, LOTW, or other logbook software

Each QSO record includes: `CALL`, `QSO_DATE`, `TIME_ON`, `MODE` (FM), `BAND`, `FREQ`, `RST_SENT`, `RST_RCVD`, `NAME`, `QTH`, and `COMMENT`.

     1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→set -e
     3→
     4→# Colors for output
     5→RED='\033[0;31m'
     6→GREEN='\033[0;32m'
     7→YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
     8→NC='\033[0m' # No Color
     9→
    10→# Load environment variables
    11→if [ -f ".env.production" ]; then
    12→    source .env.production
    13→else
    14→    echo -e "${RED}Error: .env.production file not found${NC}"
    15→    echo "Copy .env.production.example to .env.production and configure it"
    16→    exit 1
    17→fi
    18→
    19→# Validate required variables
    20→REQUIRED_VARS="DEPLOY_HOST REMOTE_DIR CONTAINER_NAME IMAGE_NAME CONTAINER_PORT SITE_URL JWT_SECRET"
    21→for var in $REQUIRED_VARS; do
    22→    if [ -z "${!var}" ]; then
    23→        echo -e "${RED}Error: $var is not set in .env.production${NC}"
    24→        exit 1
    25→    fi
    26→done
    27→
    28→# Check for --rebuild flag
    29→REBUILD_FLAG=""
    30→if [ "$1" == "--rebuild" ]; then
    31→    REBUILD_FLAG="--no-cache"
    32→    echo -e "${YELLOW}Rebuild flag set — will build without cache${NC}"
    33→fi
    34→
    35→echo -e "${GREEN}=== Deploying BOS-ARSA Log to $DEPLOY_HOST ===${NC}"
    36→echo "Host: $DEPLOY_HOST"
    37→echo "Remote dir: $REMOTE_DIR"
    38→echo "Container: $CONTAINER_NAME"
    39→echo "Port: $CONTAINER_PORT"
    40→echo ""
    41→
    42→# Step 1: Sync code to remote host
    43→echo -e "${GREEN}Step 1: Syncing code...${NC}"
    44→GIT_URL=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    45→ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    46→    if [ -d '$REMOTE_DIR' ]; then
    47→        cd '$REMOTE_DIR' && git pull
    48→    else
    49→        mkdir -p '$(dirname $REMOTE_DIR)'
    50→        git clone '$GIT_URL' '$REMOTE_DIR'
    51→    fi
    52→"
    53→
    54→# Step 2: Copy .env for docker compose
    55→echo -e "${GREEN}Step 2: Copying environment config...${NC}"
    56→ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "cat > '$REMOTE_DIR/.env' << 'ENVEOF'
    57→JWT_SECRET=$JWT_SECRET
    58→ENVEOF"
    59→
    60→# Step 3: Build Docker image on remote
    61→echo -e "${GREEN}Step 3: Building Docker image...${NC}"
    62→ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    63→    cd '$REMOTE_DIR'
    64→    docker build $REBUILD_FLAG -t '$IMAGE_NAME' .
    65→"
    66→
    67→# Step 4: Restart container (volume is preserved — data persists)
    68→echo -e "${GREEN}Step 4: Restarting container...${NC}"
    69→ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    70→    cd '$REMOTE_DIR'
    71→    docker compose up -d --force-recreate --build
    72→"
    73→
    74→# Step 5: Verify deployment
    75→echo -e "${GREEN}Step 5: Verifying deployment...${NC}"
    76→sleep 3
    77→
    78→# Check container status
    79→CONTAINER_STATUS=$(ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "docker ps --filter 'name=$CONTAINER_NAME' --format '{{.Status}}'")
    80→echo "Container status: $CONTAINER_STATUS"
    81→
    82→# Check local port
    83→LOCAL_PORT=$(echo $CONTAINER_PORT | cut -d: -f1)
    84→if ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:$LOCAL_PORT/api/v1/auth/login"; then
    85→    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Container is running on port $LOCAL_PORT${NC}"
    86→else

    93→else

   334→      <Section title="10. Tipps für die Praxis">

   336→          <li>
   337→            <b>Vor der Übung:</b> Admin erstellt die Übung, wählt die Bundesländer und aktiviert die benötigten Umsetzer.
   338→            OP-Rufzeichen pro Umsetzer eintragen.
   339→          </li>
   340→          <li>
   341→            <b>Während der Übung:</b> Alle Erfasser melden sich an und öffnen die Übung.
   342→            Rapporte werden live synchronisiert — jeder sieht sofort, was die anderen eingeben.
   343→          </li>
   344→          <li>
   345→            <b>Schnelle Eingabe:</b> Nutzen Sie Alt+1-9 für schnelle RST-Eingabe und Strg+1-9 für OE-Präfixe.
   346→            Nach Enter springt der Fokus automatisch zum nächsten Rufzeichen-Feld.
   347→          </li>
   348→          <li>
   349→            <b>Unbekannte Rufzeichen:</b> Wenn ein Rufzeichen nicht in der Datenbank ist, wird es beim Speichern
   350→            automatisch als neuer Operator angelegt.
   351→          </li>
   352→          <li>
   353→            <b>Nach der Übung:</b> Auf der Auswertungsseite können Diagramme und Textdateien exportiert werden.
   354→          </li>
   355→        </ul>
   356→      </Section>

   365→function Section({ title, children }: { title: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
   366→  return (
   367→    <section className="space-y-2">
   368→      <h2 className="text-base font-bold text-[#1e3a5f] border-b border-gray-200 pb-1">{title}</h2>
   369→      <div className="text-sm text-gray-700 space-y-2">{children}</div>
   370→    </section>
   371→  );
   372→}
   373→
   374→function Shortcut({ keys, desc }: { keys: string; desc: string }) {
   375→  return (
   376→    <tr className="border-b border-gray-100">
   377→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 font-mono text-xs whitespace-nowrap">{keys}</td>
   378→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{desc}</td>
   379→    </tr>
   380→  );
   381→}
   382→
   383→function RoleRow({ label, admin, operator }: { label: string; admin: boolean; operator: boolean }) {
   384→  return (
   385→    <tr>
   386→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{label}</td>
   387→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{admin ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   388→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{operator ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   389→    </tr>
   390→  );
   391→}

}

```
Perfect! Now I have all the information needed. Let me provide a comprehensive report on how bezirk_code is assigned to operators.

## bezirk_code Assignment Flow - Detailed Report

### 1. **Operator Schema** (`server/src/db/schema.ts`, lines 20-41)

Operators have these relevant fields:
- `bezirk_code TEXT REFERENCES bezirke(code)` (line 25)
- `bundesland_code TEXT REFERENCES bundeslaender(code)` (line 26)
- Indexed for efficient queries (line 120)

### 2. **Operator Creation - Quick-Add via POST** (`server/src/routes/operators.ts`, lines 56-78)

When creating an operator via POST `/api/v1/operators`:

```typescript
// Line 58: Destructure incoming fields
const { callsign, name, qth, bezirk_code, bundesland_code } = req.body;

// Line 64: Derive bundesland_code from callsign if not provided
const derivedBl = bundesland_code || callsignToCountryCode(callsign) || null;

// Lines 65-68: INSERT with bezirk_code passed directly from request OR null
const result = db.prepare(`
  INSERT INTO operators (callsign, name, qth, bezirk_code, bundesland_code)
  VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
`).run(callsign.toUpperCase(), name || null, qth || null, bezirk_code || null, derivedBl);
```

**Key point**: `bezirk_code` is passed from the request body or defaults to `null`. There's NO automatic assignment based on callsign—only `bundesland_code` is auto-derived.

### 3. **Operator Update - PATCH** (`server/src/routes/operators.ts`, lines 99-119)

Operators can be patched to update `bezirk_code`:

```typescript
// Line 101: List of patchable fields includes bezirk_code
const fields = ['callsign', 'name', 'qth', 'bezirk_code', 'bundesland_code', ...];

// Lines 104-108: Dynamic SQL construction for updates
for (const f of fields) {
  if (req.body[f] !== undefined) {
    updates.push(`${f} = ?`);
    params.push(f === 'callsign' ? req.body[f].toUpperCase() : req.body[f]);
  }
}

// Line 116: Execute PATCH UPDATE
db.prepare(`UPDATE operators SET ${updates.join(', ')} WHERE id = ?`).run(...params);
```

### 4. **Report Entry & Bezirk Assignment - LandMode** (`client/src/components/LandMode.tsx`, lines 112-154)

When a user enters a report in the **Bezirk row**:

```typescript
// Line 114: Get or create operator (no bezirk passed here)
const operator = await getOrCreateOperator(form.callsign, form.operator);

// Lines 118-123: AFTER operator created, immediately PATCH its bezirk_code
// This happens ASYNCHRONOUSLY and is NOT awaited
if (bezirkCode && bezirkCode !== '??') {
  apiFetch(`/api/v1/operators/${operator.id}`, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    body: JSON.stringify({ bezirk_code: bezirkCode }),
  }).catch(() => {});  // Silent catch - no error handling
}

// Lines 128-136: Create the signal report
const report = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/exercises/${exerciseId}/reports`, {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    operator_id: operator.id,
    repeater_id: repeaterId,
    ...parsed,  // readability, strength, db_over_s9
    notes: form.notes || null,
  }),
});

// Lines 138: Force bezirk_code on report object for immediate UI display
if (bezirkCode && bezirkCode !== '??') report.bezirk_code = bezirkCode;
```

**Critical observation**: The PATCH of `bezirk_code` is NOT awaited. It fires asynchronously while the report is being created.

### 5. **Report Entry & Bezirk Assignment - BundMode** (`client/src/components/BundMode.tsx`, lines 124-168)

Identical pattern:

```typescript
// Line 127: Get or create operator (no bezirk_code parameter)
const operator = await getOrCreateOperator(form.callsign, form.operator);

// Lines 131-136: ASYNC PATCH of bezirk_code (not awaited)
if (bezirkCode && bezirkCode !== '??') {
  apiFetch(`/api/v1/operators/${operator.id}`, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    body: JSON.stringify({ bezirk_code: bezirkCode }),
  }).catch(() => {});
}

// Lines 141-149: Create report (bezirk_code NOT sent in report creation)
const report = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/exercises/${exerciseId}/reports`, {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    operator_id: operator.id,
    repeater_id: repeaterId,
    ...parsed,
    notes: form.notes || null,
  }),
});

// Line 151: Force bezirk_code on report object for UI
if (bezirkCode && bezirkCode !== '??') report.bezirk_code = bezirkCode;
```

### 6. **Operator Frontend Creation - getOrCreateOperator** (`client/src/services/api.ts`, lines 1-16)

```typescript
export async function getOrCreateOperator(callsign: string, existing: any): Promise<any> {
  if (existing) return existing;  // Return cached operator if selected
  if (!callsign || callsign.length < 3) return null;
  try {
    // POST with ONLY callsign — no bezirk_code parameter
    return await apiFetch('/api/v1/operators', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ callsign: callsign.toUpperCase() }),
    });
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err.message?.includes('existiert')) {
      // Operator exists, search and return
      const results = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/operators?q=${encodeURIComponent(callsign)}`);
      return results.find((o: any) => o.callsign === callsign.toUpperCase()) || results[0] || null;
    }
    return null;
  }
}
```

## Summary of bezirk_code Assignment

| Step | Location | bezirk_code Assigned? | How |
|------|----------|----------------------|-----|

## Key Findings

1. **No automatic bezirk inference**: Unlike `bundesland_code` (which is derived from callsign prefix), `bezirk_code` has NO automatic logic. It's always explicitly set.

2. **Context-dependent assignment**: The bezirk is determined by the **row the admin enters the report in**. In LandMode, it's the Bezirk row; in BundMode, it's the Bezirk row within the Bundesland.

3. **Asynchronous PATCH**: The bezirk assignment happens in a fire-and-forget PATCH call that doesn't block report creation. If the PATCH fails silently, the operator record may not have the bezirk set, but the report is still created.

4. **UI vs. DB mismatch potential**: The report object in the frontend is forced to have `bezirk_code = bezirkCode` for display (lines 138, 151), even if the database PATCH hasn't completed yet.

     7→// Search/list operators
     8→operatorsRouter.get('/', (req, res) => {
     9→  const db = getDb();
    10→  const q = req.query.q as string;
    11→  if (q) {
    12→    const pattern = `%${q.toUpperCase()}%`;
    13→    const operators = db.prepare(`
    14→      SELECT o.*, bl.name as bundesland_name,
    15→        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signal_reports sr WHERE sr.operator_id = o.id AND sr.readability IS NOT NULL) as total_reports
    16→      FROM operators o
    17→      LEFT JOIN bundeslaender bl ON bl.code = o.bundesland_code
    18→      WHERE o.callsign LIKE ? OR UPPER(o.name) LIKE ? OR UPPER(o.qth) LIKE ?
    19→      ORDER BY o.callsign LIMIT 50
    20→    `).all(pattern, pattern, pattern);
    21→    res.json(operators);
    22→  } else {
    23→    const limit = Math.min(Math.max(parseInt(req.query.limit as string) || 100, 1), 1000);
    24→    const offset = Math.max(parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0, 0);
    25→    const operators = db.prepare('SELECT * FROM operators ORDER BY callsign LIMIT ? OFFSET ?').all(limit, offset);
    26→    const total = (db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) as c FROM operators').get() as any).c;

    28→  }
    29→});

{
  "file_path": "/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/utils/qthBezirk.ts",
  "content": "import type Database from 'better-sqlite3';\n\n/**\n * Try to derive bezirk_code from QTH (location) string.\n * Matches against bezirk names in the database, optionally filtered by bundesland.\n * Returns the bezirk_code or null if no match found.\n */\nexport function qthToBezirkCode(db: Database.Database, qth: string, bundeslandCode?: string | null): string | null {\n  if (!qth || qth.trim().length < 2) return null;\n\n  const qthNorm = qth.trim().toLowerCase();\n\n  // Get candidate bezirke (filtered by bundesland if known)\n  let bezirke: { code: string; name: string }[];\n  if (bundeslandCode) {\n    bezirke = db.prepare('SELECT code, name FROM bezirke WHERE bundesland_code = ?').all(bundeslandCode) as any[];\n  } else {\n    bezirke = db.prepare('SELECT code, name FROM bezirke').all() as any[];\n  }\n\n  // 1. Exact match (case-insensitive)\n  for (const bz of bezirke) {\n    if (bz.name.toLowerCase() === qthNorm) return bz.code;\n  }\n\n  // 2. Capital city shorthand: \"Graz\" → \"Graz Stadt\", \"Linz\" → \"Linz Stadt\", etc.\n  for (const bz of bezirke) {\n    const bzNorm = bz.name.toLowerCase();\n    if (bzNorm.endsWith(' stadt') && bzNorm.replace(' stadt', '') === qthNorm) return bz.code;\n  }\n\n  // 3. QTH starts with bezirk name or bezirk name starts with QTH (for longer names)\n  //    e.g. \"Wiener Neustadt\" matches \"Wiener Neustadt\" or \"Wiener Neustadt-Land\"\n  //    Prefer exact-length matches first (avoid \"Wels\" matching \"Wels-Land\" when \"Wels\" exists)\n  const startMatches: { code: string; name: string }[] = [];\n  for (const bz of bezirke) {\n    const bzNorm = bz.name.toLowerCase();\n    if (qthNorm.startsWith(bzNorm) || bzNorm.startsWith(qthNorm)) {\n      startMatches.push(bz);\n    }\n  }\n  if (startMatches.length === 1) return startMatches[0].code;\n  // If multiple, prefer the shorter name (more specific, e.g. \"Wels\" over \"Wels-Land\")\n  if (startMatches.length > 1) {\n    startMatches.sort((a, b) => a.name.length - b.name.length);\n    return startMatches[0].code;\n  }\n\n  return null;\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Done. Here's what changed:

**Removed**: Auto-PATCH of bezirk_code from report entry rows in LandMode and BundMode. Entering a report no longer overwrites the operator's bezirk.

**Added**: Server-side QTH-to-bezirk derivation (`server/src/utils/qthBezirk.ts`):
- On operator creation (POST): if QTH is provided and bezirk_code isn't, tries to match QTH against bezirk names (e.g. "Graz" → GC, "Mödling" → MD, "Wien" → WC)
- On operator update (PATCH): when QTH changes and bezirk_code is still null, tries to derive it
- Only auto-sets when bezirk_code is not already assigned — never overwrites manual assignments
- Matches: exact name, capital city shorthand ("Graz" → "Graz Stadt"), and prefix matches

Release v1.0.0-beta.5 recreated and deployed.

> AGENT

I understand now. Two separate concepts:

1. **Operator bezirk** (Rufzeichenliste) = where the operator lives. Should come from their address/QTH, NOT from report entry.
2. **Report bezirk** (Rapporte) = where the rapport was given. An operator can travel and report from any bezirk.

Currently both are conflated — the operator's bezirk gets overwritten by whichever row the report is entered in, and stats use the operator's bezirk. 

The fix needs:
1. Add `bezirk_code` column to `signal_reports` table — store where the rapport was given
2. Remove the PATCH that overwrites operator's bezirk from report entry
3. Update stats/display queries to use `sr.bezirk_code` instead of `o.bezirk_code`
4. Derive operator's home bezirk from QTH when possible

Let me check the schema and all affected queries first.

SELECT bl.name as bundesland, bl.code as bundesland_code, bl.sort_order as bl_sort,

## Summary of Findings

### **Critical Issues:**

1. **No bezirk field in signal_reports table** - The database schema doesn't have a `bezirk_code` column in the `signal_reports` table to store where the report was actually made from.

2. **All bezirk stats queries use operator's home bezirk** (o.bezirk_code):
   - `/api/v1/reports/stats` (lines 54-66, 83-91)
   - `/api/v1/exercises/:id/stats` (lines 113-125, 144-152, 330-342)
   - Export endpoints (export.ts lines 16-29, 65-78)

3. **Frontend workaround** - LandMode and BundMode set `report.bezirk_code` client-side only (not persisted), which makes filtering work for display but is fragile.

4. **Side effect in BundMode** - When a report is created, the operator's `bezirk_code` is updated to match the bezirk the report was entered in (BundMode.tsx line 132-135), which could incorrectly overwrite the operator's home bezirk.

### **Files That Need Changes:**

1. `/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/db/schema.ts` - Add `bezirk_code` column to `signal_reports`
2. `/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/routes/reports.ts` - All bezirk stats queries (lines 54-66, 83-91)
3. `/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/routes/exercises.ts` - All bezirk stats queries (lines 113-125, 144-152, 330-342)
4. `/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/routes/export.ts` - Export queries (lines 16-29, 65-78)
5. `/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/client/src/components/LandMode.tsx` - Remove client-side workaround (lines 117-138)
6. `/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/client/src/components/BundMode.tsx` - Remove client-side workaround and side effect (lines 131-151)

{
  "file_path": "/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/server/src/utils/qthBezirk.ts",
  "content": "import type Database from 'better-sqlite3';\n\n/**\n * Try to derive bezirk_code from QTH (location) string.\n * Matches against bezirk names in the database, optionally filtered by bundesland.\n * Returns the bezirk_code or null if no match found.\n */\nexport function qthToBezirkCode(db: Database.Database, qth: string, bundeslandCode?: string | null): string | null {\n  if (!qth || qth.trim().length < 2) return null;\n\n  const qthNorm = qth.trim().toLowerCase();\n\n  // Get candidate bezirke (filtered by bundesland if known)\n  let bezirke: { code: string; name: string }[];\n  if (bundeslandCode) {\n    bezirke = db.prepare('SELECT code, name FROM bezirke WHERE bundesland_code = ?').all(bundeslandCode) as any[];\n  } else {\n    bezirke = db.prepare('SELECT code, name FROM bezirke').all() as any[];\n  }\n\n  // 1. Exact match (case-insensitive)\n  for (const bz of bezirke) {\n    if (bz.name.toLowerCase() === qthNorm) return bz.code;\n  }\n\n  // 2. Capital city shorthand: \"Graz\" → \"Graz Stadt\", \"Linz\" → \"Linz Stadt\", etc.\n  for (const bz of bezirke) {\n    const bzNorm = bz.name.toLowerCase();\n    if (bzNorm.endsWith(' stadt') && bzNorm.replace(' stadt', '') === qthNorm) return bz.code;\n  }\n\n  // 3. QTH starts with bezirk name or bezirk name starts with QTH\n  const startMatches: { code: string; name: string }[] = [];\n  for (const bz of bezirke) {\n    const bzNorm = bz.name.toLowerCase();\n    if (qthNorm.startsWith(bzNorm) || bzNorm.startsWith(qthNorm)) {\n      startMatches.push(bz);\n    }\n  }\n  if (startMatches.length === 1) return startMatches[0].code;\n  if (startMatches.length > 1) {\n    startMatches.sort((a, b) => a.name.length - b.name.length);\n    return startMatches[0].code;\n  }\n\n  return null;\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Done. Here's a summary of what changed:

**Two separate bezirk concepts now:**
- **Operator bezirk** (`operators.bezirk_code`) = home location from Rufzeichenliste/QTH. Auto-derived from QTH when possible, otherwise set manually. Never modified by report entry.
- **Report bezirk** (`signal_reports.bezirk_code`) = where the rapport was given. Stored on each report from the UI row context. Used for all stats, charts, and exports.

**Changes:**
- `signal_reports` table gets its own `bezirk_code` column (existing data backfilled from operator)
- Report creation sends `bezirk_code` from the UI row
- No more auto-PATCH of operator bezirk on report entry
- All stats/export queries use `sr.bezirk_code` instead of `o.bezirk_code`
- Operator QTH-to-bezirk derivation on create/update (for home bezirk)

## Complete Excel Workbook Analysis

**File:** `2026 BOS-ARSA - Krisenkommunikationsuebung.xlsx` (14.9 MB)
**Total sheets:** 7

---

### 1. Sheet List and Purposes

| # | Sheet Name | Purpose | Dimensions |
|---|-----------|---------|------------|
| 1 | `Gesamtuebersicht` | Yearly summary - one row per Sunday with participant + report counts | 53 rows x 26 cols |
| 2 | `20260104` | Exercise 2026-01-04 | 1280 rows x 247 cols |
| 3 | `20260111` | Exercise 2026-01-11 | 1281 rows x 247 cols |
| 4 | `20260118` | Exercise 2026-01-18 | 1282 rows x 247 cols |
| 5 | `20260125` | Exercise 2026-01-25 | 1287 rows x 247 cols |
| 6 | `20260201` | Exercise 2026-02-01 | 1291 rows x 247 cols |
| 7 | `20260208` | Exercise 2026-02-08 | 1294 rows x 247 cols |

Sheet names are `YYYYMMDD` dates (the Saturday before the Sunday exercise, since dates are stored as `T23:00:00Z`, i.e. midnight CET = Sunday).

---

### 2. Gesamtuebersicht (Summary Sheet)

Simple 3-column layout:

| Column | Content |
|--------|---------|
| A | Date (ISO timestamp, one per Sunday for the full year) |
| B | Teilnehmer*innen (participant count) |
| C | Rapporte (total report count) |

Row 53 has year totals in B and C. There are also quarterly subtotals in columns D/E at rows 14, 27, 28, 40, 52. Pre-populated with all Sundays for 2026 (52 rows); only the first 6 have data filled in.

---

### 3. Exercise Sheet Column Layout (Identical Across All 6 Sheets)

The exercise sheets have a **master operator list** in rows 2-~1062 (growing each week as new operators are added) with the following column groups:

#### A. Operator Information Columns (A-O)

| Col | Header | Content | Example |
|-----|--------|---------|---------|
| A | Rufzeichen | Callsign | `OE8OPT`, `OE/F4HHF`, `S55UJE` |
| B | Zusatz | Suffix (portable, mobile) | `p`, `/p`, `mobil`, `m` |
| C | Anwesend 1 | Attendance flag (redundant with D) | `1` or ` ` |
| D | Anwesend | Attendance: `1` = present, `0` = absent | `0` or `1` |
| E | BOS-ARSA Mitgl | BOS-ARSA membership | (number) |
| F | Geschlecht | Gender | (value) |
| G | Mail | Email | (value) |
| H | A.R.E.N.A | ARENA membership | (value) |
| I | Portable Verfuegbarkeit | Portable availability | (value) |
| J | Name | First name | `Manfred`, `Patrick` |
| K | QTH | Location | `Wien 12`, `Salzburg`, `Schwechat` |
| L | Bez-Kenner | Bezirk code (2-3 letters) | `WC`, `SC`, `BL`, `VK` |
| M | Bundesland | State with number prefix | `01-Wien`, `02-Salzburg`, `08-Kaernten` |
| N | Uebungs-unterstuetzung | Exercise support role | (value) |
| O | safeReach | safeReach alerting status | (value) |

#### B. Repeater/Frequency Report Columns (P-Z) -- THE KEY DATA

These 11 columns each represent one repeater or direct frequency. **Each cell contains an RST signal report string or is empty.** The same 11 repeaters are used across all 6 exercise sheets; only the OP (net control operator) name varies week-to-week in columns P, U, and Z.

| Col | Repeater Name | Frequency | Band | Callsign | Notes |
|-----|--------------|-----------|------|----------|-------|
| P | Gerlitze 2m | 145.7625 MHz, -0.6 offset | 2m | OE8XNK | OP varies: OE8SSR/OE8GWQ/OE8HAM |
| Q | Gerlitze 70cm | 439.050 MHz, -7.6, CTCSS 88.5 | 70cm | OE8GWQ (same site) | |
| R | OE-Link (Magdalensberg, Hermannskogel, Schoeckl, Gaisberg) | 438.575 MHz, -7.6, CTCSS 88.5 | 70cm | OE8XMK | **Linked repeater** - the most used! |
| S | Buschberg | 438.800 MHz | 70cm | OE3KDS | |
| T | Direktfrequenz | 145.300 MHz | 2m | OE3EGH | Direct frequency, not a repeater |
| U | Goldeck 2m | 145.650 MHz, -0.6, CTCSS 88.5 | 2m | OE8XOK | OP varies |
| V | Dobratsch 23cm | 1298.150 MHz | 23cm | OE8GWQ | |
| W | Struska 70cm | 439.325 MHz, -7.6, CTCSS 123 | 70cm | S55UJE | Slovenian repeater |
| X | Hochstuhl | 439.3625 MHz, -7.6, CTCSS 123 | 70cm | OE8KKK | |
| Y | Zirbitzkogel | 438.800 MHz | 70cm | OE3EGH | |
| Z | Direkte 145.525 | 145.525 MHz | 2m | OE8OPT/OE8HAM | Direct frequency |

**Column R (OE-Link) is by far the most used repeater** -- on 2026-01-04, 85 of 98 reports were on this repeater. On 2026-02-01, 109 of 179 reports.

#### C. Report Count Column (AA)

| Col | Header | Content |
|-----|--------|---------|
| AA | Anzahl der Rapporte | Count of reports for this operator in this exercise |

#### D. First Bezirk Block (AB-DY, cols 27-128) -- "Registration per Bezirk"

~102 columns, each headed with a **Bezirk code** (WC, HU, CZ, SLO, SC, FK, FE, AM, SB, HE, KC, GD, ...). Values are `1` for every operator registered in that Bezirk. This is essentially a **lookup/pivot** -- each operator has a `1` in the column matching their `Bez-Kenner` (col L). This is a pre-computed matrix, NOT import-relevant data.

Some special codes: `D` (Deutschland), `IT` (Italien), `HU` (Ungarn), `SLO` (Slowenien), `CH` (Schweiz), `CZ` (Tschechien), `Slowakei`, `HR` (Kroatien), `LST` (Liechtenstein).

#### E. Second Bezirk Block (DZ-HY, cols 129-232) -- "Report per Bezirk"

| Col | Header | Content |
|-----|--------|---------|
| DZ | Rapporte | Report count for this row (same as AA) |
| EA | OM | (mostly blank) |
| EB-HY | Bezirk codes with numeric suffixes (WC4, HU2, CZ5, SC7, etc.) | `1` if this operator submitted a report AND is from that Bezirk |

This is another **pre-computed pivot matrix** -- marks which Bezirk a report came from. Not needed for import.

---

### 5. Row Structure Summary

Each exercise sheet:
- **Row 1:** Headers
- **Rows 2-~1062:** Operator master list (ALL known operators, whether they participated or not)
  - `D=1` means they participated this week; `D=0` means they are in the master list but did not participate
  - Columns P-Z contain the RST reports (only for participating operators)
- **Row ~1063:** Summary/totals row (column A = total operator count, K = "Gesamt:", P-Z = per-repeater report counts)
- **Row ~1064:** "Anwesend" count
- **Rows ~1065-~1153:** Per-Bezirk breakdown (format: J="Bundesland Bezirk", K=station count, L=report count)

---

### 6. Key Findings for Import

**What to import from each exercise sheet:**

1. **Exercise metadata:** Derive from sheet name (YYYYMMDD)
2. **Active repeaters:** Parse from row 1 headers in columns P-Z (including the OP name which varies)
3. **Operator data:** From columns A, B, J, K, L, M for rows where D=1
4. **Signal reports:** From columns P-Z for each operator row where D=1

**Problems and challenges for import:**

1. **No merged cells** -- this is good, clean structure.
2. **Report format is free-text** -- not standardized RST. There are comma-separated multi-reports in a single cell (e.g., `"3/5 NBST, 5/9 HK, 5/9 JAU"`), reports with parenthetical notes, and "OP" markers mixed with signal values.
3. **Date parsing:** The Excel dates store as the day before at 23:00 UTC (e.g., `2026-01-03T23:00:00.000Z` = Jan 4 exercise). Need to add 1 day or parse in CET.
4. **Repeater headers are complex strings** that need parsing to extract: name, frequency, offset, CTCSS, band, repeater callsign, and OP callsign.
5. **The OP callsign changes week to week** embedded in the header text (cols P, U, Z vary). An import needs to extract this per-sheet.
6. **One spurious date value found:** In sheet 20260208, OE8AWZ's Goldeck report cell contains a JavaScript Date object (`Sat Dec 30 1899`) -- likely a number that got misinterpreted as a date by Excel. The original value was probably an RST report.
7. **Rows grow each week** as new operators are added (1015 -> 1016 -> 1017 -> 1021 -> 1025 -> 1026). Operators are never removed.
8. **Non-Austrian callsigns** are present: S55UJE (Slovenia), HB9/HB0 (Switzerland/Liechtenstein), DO8 (Germany), IV3/IW4 (Italy), OM4 (Slovakia), 9A5 (Croatia), HA6 (Hungary).
9. **The bezirk columns (AB-HY) and equipment columns (HZ-IL) are supplementary metadata** -- the bezirk columns are pre-computed pivots and should NOT be imported as separate data. The equipment columns are static operator attributes.
10. **Summary rows at the bottom** (after the last operator) contain per-Bezirk stats and can be skipped during import.

**Recommended import column mapping:**

| Excel Column | Maps to DB Field |
|-------------|-----------------|
| A | operator.callsign |
| B | operator.suffix (portable/mobile) |
| D | report.present (boolean: 1 = participated) |
| J | operator.name |
| K | operator.qth |
| L | operator.bezirk_code |
| M | operator.bundesland |
| P-Z (cell value) | report.rst_raw (free text signal report) |
| P-Z (header) | repeater definition (needs parsing) |
| Sheet name | exercise.date |

Here's the full analysis:

## Excel Structure

**7 sheets**: 1 summary (`Gesamtübersicht`) + 6 exercise sheets (`20260104` through `20260208`)

Each exercise sheet has **~1060 operator rows** (the full master list, `D=1` = participated) and **11 repeater columns** (P–Z), with RST reports in cells.

### Column Layout

| Cols | Content |
|------|---------|
| A | Rufzeichen |
| B | Suffix (/P, /M) |
| D | Anwesend (1/0) |
| J | Name |
| K | QTH |
| L | Bez-Kenner (bezirk code) |
| M | Bundesland (e.g. "01-Wien") |
| P–Z | 11 repeater columns, each cell = RST report string |
| AB–HY | Pre-computed bezirk pivot matrices (skip) |
| HZ–IL | Equipment data (Gerät, Antenne, Notstrom, etc.) |

### Problems for Import

**1. Free-text RST format** — The biggest challenge. Report cells aren't standardized:
- `5/9 HK` — normal
- `5/9+60 FK` — with dB and einstiegspunkt
- `3/5 NBST, 5/9 HK, 5/9 JAU` — **multiple reports in one cell** (comma-separated, different einstiegspunkte)
- `OP` — net control marker
- `5/9+35 OP` — report AND operator marker combined
- `5/9+40 (zu OE8GWQ)` — free-text notes mixed in

**2. Repeater headers are complex strings** — e.g. `"MAGDALENSBERG, HERMANNSKOGEL, SCHÖCKL, GAISBERG -70CM OE8XMK 438.575 /-7,6 SAT 88,5 HZ OP: OE8SSR"`. Need parsing for name, frequency, offset, CTCSS, callsign, and OP (which changes per sheet).

**3. Multi-report cells** — One cell can contain reports for multiple einstiegspunkte of the OE-Link. Currently our DB has a 1:1 relationship (one report per operator per repeater). These would need to be split or the "best" report taken.

**4. Date encoding** — Sheet names are `YYYYMMDD` but Excel dates are stored as UTC midnight-1h (Saturday 23:00 = Sunday CET).

**5. Growing row count** — Operators are appended each week (1015→1026 rows), never removed. Import needs upsert logic.

**6. Sporadic data corruption** — One cell has an Excel date value where an RST was expected.

### What's Feasible

An import **is possible** but requires:
- A robust RST parser that handles all the free-text variations
- Multi-report cell splitting (comma-separated)
- OP marker extraction
- Repeater header parsing
- Upsert logic for operators (match by callsign)
- The UNIQUE constraint (exercise + operator + repeater) means multi-report cells need special handling

The operator data (callsign, name, QTH, bezirk, bundesland, equipment) is cleanly structured and easy to import. The signal reports are the hard part due to the free-text format.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Load environment variables
if [ -f ".env.production" ]; then
    source .env.production
else
    echo -e "${RED}Error: .env.production file not found${NC}"
    echo "Copy .env.production.example to .env.production and configure it"
    exit 1
fi

# Validate required variables
REQUIRED_VARS="DEPLOY_HOST REMOTE_DIR CONTAINER_NAME IMAGE_NAME CONTAINER_PORT SITE_URL JWT_SECRET"
for var in $REQUIRED_VARS; do
    if [ -z "${!var}" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Error: $var is not set in .env.production${NC}"
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Check for --rebuild flag
REBUILD_FLAG=""
if [ "$1" == "--rebuild" ]; then
    REBUILD_FLAG="--no-cache"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Rebuild flag set — will build without cache${NC}"
fi

echo -e "${GREEN}=== Deploying BOS-ARSA Log to $DEPLOY_HOST ===${NC}"
echo "Host: $DEPLOY_HOST"
echo "Remote dir: $REMOTE_DIR"
echo "Container: $CONTAINER_NAME"
echo "Port: $CONTAINER_PORT"
echo ""

# Step 1: Sync code to remote host
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 1: Syncing code...${NC}"
GIT_URL=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo "")
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    if [ -d '$REMOTE_DIR' ]; then
        cd '$REMOTE_DIR' && git pull
    else
        mkdir -p '$(dirname $REMOTE_DIR)'
        git clone '$GIT_URL' '$REMOTE_DIR'
    fi
"

# Step 2: Copy .env for docker compose
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 2: Copying environment config...${NC}"
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "cat > '$REMOTE_DIR/.env' << 'ENVEOF'
JWT_SECRET=$JWT_SECRET
ENVEOF"

# Step 3: Build Docker image on remote
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 3: Building Docker image...${NC}"
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    cd '$REMOTE_DIR'
    docker build $REBUILD_FLAG -t '$IMAGE_NAME' .
"

# Step 4: Restart container (volume is preserved — data persists)
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 4: Restarting container...${NC}"
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    cd '$REMOTE_DIR'
    docker compose up -d --force-recreate --build
"

# Step 5: Verify deployment
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 5: Verifying deployment...${NC}"
sleep 3

# Check container status
CONTAINER_STATUS=$(ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "docker ps --filter 'name=$CONTAINER_NAME' --format '{{.Status}}'")
echo "Container status: $CONTAINER_STATUS"

# Check local port
LOCAL_PORT=$(echo $CONTAINER_PORT | cut -d: -f1)
if ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:$LOCAL_PORT/api/v1/auth/login"; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Container is running on port $LOCAL_PORT${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Container not yet responding on port $LOCAL_PORT — may still be starting${NC}"
fi

# Check public URL
if curl -sf -o /dev/null "$SITE_URL" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Site is accessible at $SITE_URL${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Public URL not yet accessible — configure Cloudflare tunnel${NC}"
fi

echo ""
echo -e "${GREEN}=== Deployment complete ===${NC}"
echo ""
echo "To seed a fresh database:  docker exec $CONTAINER_NAME node dist/server/db/seed.js"
```

Here's the full comparison:

### Excel vs DB Data

| Date | Excel (Attendees / Reports) | DB (Participants / Reports) | Status |
|------|------|------|------|
| 2026-01-04 | 88 / ~286 | 13 / 13 | Partial |
| 2026-01-07 | — | 26 / 26 | DB only (no Excel sheet) |
| 2026-01-11 | 79 / ~270 | — | Missing from DB |
| 2026-01-18 | 91 / ~312 | 101 / 120 | Partial |
| 2026-01-25 | 113 / ~380 | — | Missing from DB |
| 2026-02-01 | 126 / ~407 | — | Missing from DB |
| 2026-02-04 | — | 20 / 20 | DB only (no Excel sheet) |
| 2026-02-08 | 86 / ~315 | 56 / 64 | Partial |
| 2026-02-09 to 2026-02-16 | — | — | Not covered |

**Summary:**
- The **Excel covers 6 Sundays** (Jan 4 – Feb 8), with 88–126 attendees each
- The **DB has 64 exercises** pre-created for the whole year (Jan 4 – Dec 27), but only **5 have any data** — and those have significantly fewer entries than the Excel (e.g. Jan 4: 13 in DB vs 88 in Excel)
- **3 Excel dates are completely missing from DB** (Jan 11, Jan 25, Feb 1)
- **2 DB dates don't match any Excel sheet** (Jan 7 and Feb 4 — likely test data)
- **No data at all from Feb 9 onwards** — so last Sunday (Feb 16) is not covered
- The DB entries that do exist appear to be partial test imports, not the full Excel data

The data does **not** cover the whole year — only scattered partial entries from the first 5 weeks.

String(row[c]).trim() : \\\"\\\";\n      if (!val || val === \\\"0\\\") continue;\n      allReports.push(val);\n      \n      // Try parse RST\n      const isOp = val.toUpperCase().startsWith(\\\"OP\\\");\n      const cleaned = val.replace(/^OP\\\\s*/i, \\\"\\\").trim();\n      \n      // Match R/S pattern\n      const m = cleaned.match(/^(\\\\d)\\\\/(\\\\d)(\\\\+{1,2}|\\\\+\\\\d+)?\\\\s*(.*)/);\n      if (m) {\n        const [, r, s, db, suffix] = m;\n        const sfx = suffix ? suffix.trim() : \\\"\\\";\n        if (sfx) allAbbreviations.add(sfx);\n        rstFormats.add((isOp ? \\\"OP \\\" : \\\"\\\") + \\\"R/S\\\" + (db || \\\"\\\") + (sfx ? \\\" +suffix\\\" : \\\"\\\"));\n      } else if (!isOp || cleaned) {\n        rstFormats.add(val.substring(0, 30));\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nconsole.log(\\\"Total report cells across all sheets: \\\" + allReports.length);\nconsole.log(\\\"\\\\n=== RST formats found ===\\\");\n[...rstFormats].sort().forEach(f => console.log(\\\"  \\\" + f));\nconsole.log(\\\"\\\\n=== Location abbreviations found ===\\\");\n[...allAbbreviations].sort().forEach(a => console.log(\\\"  \\\" + a));\n\"' 2>&1",

String(row[c]).trim() : \\\"\\\";\n      if (!val || val === \\\"0\\\") continue;\n      \n      // Multi-report: has comma followed by another R/S pattern\n      if (val.includes(\\\",\\\") && /\\\\d\\\\/\\\\d/.test(val)) {\n        multiCells.push(name + \\\" | \\\" + cs + \\\" [\\\" + c + \\\"]: \\\" + val);\n      } else if (/^(OP\\\\s*)?\\\\d\\\\/\\\\d/.test(val) || val === \\\"OP\\\") {\n        pureCells.push(val);\n      } else {\n        weirdCells.push(name + \\\" | \\\" + cs + \\\" [\\\" + c + \\\"]: \\\" + val);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nconsole.log(\\\"=== Pure standard reports: \\\" + pureCells.length);\nconsole.log(\\\"=== Multi-report cells: \\\" + multiCells.length);\nmultiCells.forEach(m => console.log(\\\"  \\\" + m));\nconsole.log(\\\"\\\\n=== Non-standard / weird cells: \\\" + weirdCells.length);\nweirdCells.forEach(w => console.log(\\\"  \\\" + w));\n\"' 2>&1",

Here's the comprehensive analysis:

## Analysis: Excel Import Feasibility

### Data Overview
- **8 sheets**: 7 exercise sheets + 1 "Gesamtübersicht" (summary)
- **7 exercises**: Jan 4, 11, 18, 25, Feb 1, 8, 15 (2026)
- **~1280-1294 operator rows per sheet**, ~80-130 actually attended each week
- **11 repeater columns** (P-Z, cols 15-25)
- **~906 signal report cells** total → after splitting multi-report cells, roughly **~950 individual reports**

### Structure per sheet (247 columns!)

| Cols | Purpose | Importable? |
|------|---------|-------------|
| 0 (A) | Rufzeichen | Yes — operator lookup |
| 1 (B) | Zusatz (suffix like "mobil") | Notes field |
| 3 (D) | Anwesend (0/1) | Yes — attendance |
| 9 (J) | Name | Yes — operator metadata |
| 10 (K) | QTH | Yes — operator metadata |
| 11 (L) | Bez-Kenner (bezirk code) | Yes — bezirk_code for reports |
| 12 (M) | Bundesland | Yes — operator metadata |
| 15-25 (P-Z) | **Signal reports per repeater** | Yes — main import target |
| 26 (AA) | Anzahl der Rapporte (count) | Computed, skip |
| 27-128 | Bezirk presence matrix | Skip (1/0 flags) |
| 129-232 | Duplicate bezirk tracking | Skip |
| 233-245 | Equipment, coordinates, etc. | Possible future use |

### Repeater Column → DB Mapping (all 11 map cleanly!)

| Col | Excel Header | DB ID | DB short_name |
|-----|-------------|-------|---------------|
| 15 | Gerlitze 2m OE8XNK 145.7625 | 265 | Gerlitzen 2m |
| 16 | Gerlitze 70cm 439.050 | 266 | Gerlitzen 70cm |
| 17 | Magdalensberg linked OE8XMK 438.575 | 267 | Magdalensberg linked |
| 18 | Buschberg 438.800 | 226 | Buschberg 70cm |
| 19 | Direktfrequenz 145.300 | 283 | Direkte 145.300 |
| 20 | Goldeck 2m OE8XOK 145.650 | 269 | Goldeck 2m |
| 21 | Dobratsch 23cm 1298.150 | 274 | Dobratsch 23cm |
| 22 | Struška 70cm S55UJE 439.325 | 278 | Struška 70cm |
| 23 | Hochstuhl 439.3625 | 279 | Hochstuhl 70cm |
| 24 | Zirbitzkogel 438.800 | 249 | Zirbitzkogel 70cm |
| 25 | 145.525 Direkte | 281 | Direkte 145.525 |

### Signal Report Format Analysis

**853 standard reports** (94%) match `R/S[+dB] [Einstiegspunkt]`:
- `5/9+30 HK` → R=5, S=9, dB=+30, EP=Hermannskogel
- `5/9++ GB` → R=5, S=9, dB="++", EP=Gaisberg
- `5/9 HK` → R=5, S=9, EP=Hermannskogel
- `OP` → pure OP marker

**21 multi-report cells** (2.3%) — comma-separated, e.g.:
- `5/9+20 HK, 5/9+20 BR, 5/5 JAU, 4/3 FK` → 4 separate reports for 4 einstiegspunkte

**~18 summary/total rows** — the last row per sheet (callsign is a number like "1064") → just skip

**3 truly weird cells**: `OP BR`, `579+20 SCHÖ`, `pc` → handle with fallback

### Einstiegspunkt Mapping (for linked repeater OE8XMK, col 17)

| Excel Abbreviation | DB ID | DB site_name | Status |
|-------------------|-------|-------------|--------|
| HK | 49 | Hermannskogel | Exists |
| GB | 50 | Gaisberg | Exists |
| NBST | 51 | Nebelstein | Exists |
| JAU/Jau | 52 | Jauerling | Exists |
| FK | 53 | Feuerkogel | Exists |
| SCHÖ | 54 | Schöckl | Exists |
| LT | 55 | Lachtal | Exists |
| DO | 60 | Dornbirn | Exists |
| Hochstein/HOCHS | 57 | Hochstein | Exists |
| Ahorn | 58 | Ahorn | Exists |
| MK/MGDB/Mgdb | 59 | Magdalensberg | Exists |
| BR/BrR/Brentenriegel | **MISSING** | Brentenriegel | **Need to add** |
| PATSCH/PaK/PK | **MISSING** | Patscherkofel | **Need to add** |
| eR | **MISSING** | ? | Unknown |

### Verdict: **YES, import is very feasible**

~94% of data parses cleanly. The remaining ~6% (multi-reports, edge cases) requires comma splitting and minor special-case handling. The import would need to:

1. **Add 2-3 missing einstiegspunkte** (Brentenriegel, Patscherkofel)
2. **Delete existing partial data** for exercises that already have entries (Jan 4, 18, Feb 8)
3. **Match operators by callsign** — 6000+ already in DB from the Rufzeichen import
4. **Parse RST** with regex, split comma-separated cells
5. **Map bezirk** from column L for report-level bezirk_code

String(header).match(/auf\\s+(\\S+)/);\n  if (m2) return m2[1];\n  return null;\n}\n\n// --- RST Parser ---\n\nfunction parseReportCell(rawValue, colIndex) {\n  const val = String(rawValue).trim();\n  if (!val || val === '0') return [];\n\n  // Split multi-report cells: \"5/9+20 HK, 5/9+20 BR, 5/5 JAU\"\n  const parts = val.split(/,\\s*(?=\\d|OP)/i);\n  const results = [];\n  for (const part of parts) {\n    const parsed = parseSingleRst(part.trim(), colIndex);\n    if (parsed) results.push(parsed);\n  }\n  return results;\n}\n\nfunction parseSingleRst(raw, colIndex) {\n  if (!raw) return null;\n  let val = raw;\n  let isOp = false;\n\n  // Pure OP\n  if (/^OP$/i.test(val)) {\n    return { isOp: true, readability: null, strength: null, dbOverS9: null, ep: null, notes: null, original: \"5/9+60 GB OP\"\n  if (/\\s+-\\s*OP$/i.test(val)) {\n    isOp = true;\n    val = val.replace(/\\s+-\\s*OP$/i, '');\n  } else if (/\\s+OP$/i.test(val)) {\n    isOp = true;\n    val = val.replace(/\\s+OP$/i, '');\n  }\n  // \"(OP)\" suffix\n  if (/\\s*\\(OP\\)\\s*$/i.test(val)) {\n    isOp = true;\n    val = val.replace(/\\s*\\(OP\\)\\s*$/i, '');\n  }\n\n  // Standard RST: \"5/9\", repeater, suffix is einstiegspunkt + optional notes\n      const parenMatch = suffix.match(/\\(.*?\\)/);\n      let clean = suffix.replace(/\\s*\\(.*?\\)\\s*/g, '').trim();\n      // Remove trailing      notes = suffix;\n    }\n\n    return { isOp, readability, strength, dbOverS9, ep, notes, original: raw };\n  }\n\n  // No-slash format: \"579+20 SCHÖ\" → best guess R=5, S=9, dB=+20\n  const m2 = dbOverS9, ep, notes: notes.trim(), original: raw };\n  }\n\n  // OP with just an abbreviation: \"BR\" after OP was stripped\n  if (isOp && val && !val.match(/\\d/)) {\n    let ep = (colIndex === 17) ? dbOverS9: null, ep: null, notes: raw, original: raw };\n}\n\n// --- Main ---\n\nconst xlsxPath = process.argv[2];\nconst outputDir = process.argv[3] || '/tmp';\n\nif (!xlsxPath) {\n  console.error('Usage: node parse-excel-to-json.js <xlsx-path> [output-dir]');\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nconsole.log('Reading Excel:', xlsxPath);\nconst wb = XLSX.readFile(xlsxPath);\nconsole.log('Sheets:', wb.SheetNames.join(', '));\n\nconst exercises = [];\nconst operatorUpdates = {}; // callsign → { name, qth, ... }\nconst report = [];\nlet totalReports = 0;\nlet totalAttendees = 0;\nlet parseErrors = [];\n\nfor (const sheetName of wb.SheetNames) {\n  if (!sheetName.match(/^\\d{8}$/)) continue; // Skip non-exercise sheets\n\n  const dateStr = [];\n\n  // Extract OP callsigns from repeater headers\n  const repeaterSetup = [];\n  for (const [colStr, rep] of Object.entries(REPEATER_MAP)) {\n    const col = parseInt(colStr);\n    const headerVal = header[col] ? String(header[col]) : '';\n    const opCallsign = extractOpCallsign(headerVal);\n    repeaterSetup.push({\n      repeaterId: rep.id,\n      repeaterName: rep.name,\n      operatorCallsign: opCallsign,\n      headerText: headerVal.substring(0, 80),\n    });\n  }\n\n  const attendance = [];\n  const reports = [];\n  let sheetAttendees = 0;\n  let sheetReports = 0;\n  let sheetOps = 0;\n  let sheetMultiCells = 0;\n  let sheetUnparsed = 0;\n  const perRepeater = {};\n  const perEp = {};\n\n  for (let i = 1; i < data.length; i++) {\n    const row = data[i];\n    if (!row || !row[0]) continue;\n\n    const callsign = String(row[0]).trim().toUpperCase();\n\n    // Skip summary/total rows (callsign is purely numeric)\n    if (/^\\d+$/.test(callsign)) continue;\n\n    // Skip empty or invalid callsigns\n    if (callsign.length < 3) continue;\n\n    const attended = row[3] && parseInt(String(row[3])) > 0;\n    if (!attended) continue;\n\n    sheetAttendees++;\n\n    const suffix = row[1] ?         id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        exercise_id TEXT REFERENCES "exercises"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

CREATE TABLE operators (

      callsign TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,

    )

const exMissingOps = [];\n\n  // Group reports by callsign\n  const reportsByCallsign = {};\n  for (const r of exercise.reports) {\n    if (!reportsByCallsign[r.callsign]) opData.isExerciseSupport || 0,\n          opData.gender || null,\n          opData.email || null,\n          opData.equipment || null,\n          opData.antenna || null,\n          opData.hasEmergencyPower || 0,\n          opData.hasLighthouseReadiness || 0,\n          opData.latitude || null,\n          opData.longitude || null,\n          now, now\n        );\n        operatorId = Number(result.lastInsertRowid);\n        operatorMap[cs] = operatorId;\n        exNewOps++;\n        exMissingOps.push(cs);\n      } catch (e) {\n        if (e.message && }\n    }\n  }\n\n  grandTotalAttendees += exAttendees;\n  grandTotalReports += exReports;\n  grandTotalNewOperators += exNewOps;\n  grandTotalMerged += exMerged;\n\n  report.push(`  Teilnehmer:     ${exAttendees}`);\n  report.push(`  Rapporte:       ${exReports} (davon ${exOpMarkers} OP-Marker)`);\n  if (exMerged > 0) {\n    report.push(`  Zusammengeführt: ${exMerged} Multi-EP-Rapporte in Notes   "content": "const Database = require('/app/node_modules/better-sqlite3');\nconst fs = require('fs');\n\nconst records = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/tmp/rufzeichen.json', 'utf-8'));\nconsole.log('Records to import:', records.length);\n\nconst PREFIX_MAP = [\n  [/^OE1/, '01'], [/^OE2/, '02'], [/^OE3/, '03'], [/^OE4/, '04'], [/^OE5/, '05'],\n  [/^OE6/, '06'], [/^OE7/, '07'], [/^OE8/, '08'], [/^OE9/, '09'],\n];\nfunction toBlCode(cs) {\n  for (const [re, code] of PREFIX_MAP) { if (re.test(cs)) return code; }\n  return null;\n}\n\nconst db = new Database('/data/bosarsalog.db');\ndb.pragma('journal_mode = WAL');\ndb.pragma('foreign_keys = ON');\n\nconst selectOp = db.prepare('SELECT id, name, qth FROM operators WHERE callsign = ?');\nconst insertOp = db.prepare(\"INSERT INTO operators (callsign, name, qth, bundesland_code, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'))\");\nconst updateOp = db.prepare(\"UPDATE operators SET name = ?, qth = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE callsign = ?\");\n\nlet inserted = 0, updated = 0, skipped = 0;\n\nconst importAll = db.transaction(() => {\n  for (const rec of records) {\n    const existing = selectOp.get(rec.callsign);\n    if (existing) {\n      if (existing.name !== rec.name || existing.qth !== rec.qth) {\n        updateOp.run(rec.name, rec.qth, rec.callsign);\n        updated++;\n      } else {\n        skipped++;\n      }\n    } else {\n      insertOp.run(rec.callsign, rec.name, rec.qth, toBlCode(rec.callsign));\n      inserted++;\n    }\n  }\n});\nimportAll();\n\nconsole.log('Inserted:', inserted);\nconsole.log('Updated:', updated);\nconsole.log('Skipped:', skipped);\nconsole.log('Total operators now:', db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) as c FROM operators').get().c);\ndb.close();\n"
